Plug in your tablet soon.

sentences: Maya is drawing a comic on the computer.
She taps the trash can by mistake.

visual.title: Delete this file?
rows: Delete 'Comic Page 3'?
You cannot get it back.

passages.title: The Microwave Label
sentences: Ben wants to heat his soup in the microwave.
He reads the label on the door.

visual.title: Microwave Safety
rows: No metal in the microwave.
Use a bowl that says microwave safe.
Ask an adult if you are not sure.

passages.title: The Location Box
sentences: Sam gets a new map app called Trail Tracker.
When he opens it, a box pops up.

visual.title: Allow Trail Tracker to use your location?
rows: Trail Tracker wants to know where you are.
It will show your place on the trail map.

passages.title: Unsaved Changes
sentences: Priya is writing a plan for her rover.
She clicks the X to close the file.

visual.title: Unsaved changes
rows: You changed 'Rover Plan'.
Save your changes before closing?

passages.title: Update Ready
sentences: Ben turns on his tablet to play Block Builder.
A box pops up.

visual.title: Update ready
rows: A new update for Block Builder is ready.
It takes about 10 minutes.
Plug in your tablet before you update.

passages.title: The Prize Pop-Up
sentences: Leo is watching a skateboard video on his tablet.
A bright box pops up over the video.
It flashes and plays a loud sound.

visual.title: YOU WON!
rows: Congratulations! You won a free game console!
Tap Claim Prize in the next 60 seconds.
Type your name and home address to get your prize.

passages.title: A Chat About Gems
sentences: Ben is playing Block Builder online.
A player Ben has never met sends him a chat.

rows: Hi Ben! I am on your Block Builder team.
I can give you 500 free gems.
Just send me your password.
Hurry! This offer ends today.

passages.title: Our Tablet Rules
sentences: The Rivera family has tablet rules on the fridge.
Sam reads them before he plays.

visual.title: Our Tablet Rules
rows: You can tap OK on a low battery box.
You can tap Save to keep your work.
Ask an adult before you tap Allow on any app.
Ask an adult before you buy anything.
Never share a password. Tell an adult if someone asks for it.
Close any box that says you won a prize. Then tell an adult.

passages.title: Headphone Safety
sentences: Sam is listening to a podcast about trains on his tablet.
He is wearing headphones when this box pops up.

visual.title: Headphone Safety
rows: You have listened at a high volume for 1 hour today.
Loud sound for a long time can hurt your hearing.
If you do nothing, the volume will go down by itself in 30 seconds.
You can turn it up again later, but a lower volume is safer for your ears.

passages.title: SketchCove Privacy Settings
sentences: Maya gets a new drawing app called SketchCove.
Before she posts a comic, she opens the privacy settings with her mom.

Everyone

passages.title: The Gem Shop
sentences: Ben is playing Block Builder on the family tablet.
He taps the gem shop, and this box opens.

visual.title: Gem Shop: Buy Gems?
rows: Gems buy new skins and tools in Block Builder.
Small pack: 100 gems for $1.
Big pack: 500 gems for $4. Best value!
This is real money. It is charged to the card saved on this tablet.
Players under 13 need a parent to approve each purchase.
Tap Ask a Parent to send a request. Nothing is charged until a parent says yes.
Gems cannot be traded back for money after you buy them.
Free gems: finish the Daily Build to earn 20 gems each day.
You have 40 gems now. The Rocket Drill tool costs 100 gems.

passages.title: The Sign-In Code
sentences: Ben's family phone gets this text from Block Builder.
Ben plays Block Builder on a laptop and on a tablet.

rows: Your Block Builder sign-in code is 482913.
Someone is signing in to Ben's account on a new laptop in Harbor Town.
If this is you, type the code on the sign-in screen. The code stops working in 10 minutes.
Never tell this code to anyone. Block Builder staff will never ask you for it in a chat, a call or an email.
If this is not you, do not type the code anywhere. Tap Secure My Account in the app and change your password with an adult.
Each code works one time only. A new sign-in needs a new code.

passages.title: An Email About Priya's Account
sentences: Priya gets an email on the family computer.
She buys rover parts from a shop called RoboParts.

visual.subject: URGENT: Your account will be closed in 24 hours!
rows: Dear Customer,
Our safety system found strange activity on your RoboParts account last night.
We are sorry for the trouble, and we want to keep your account safe.
Your account will be closed in 24 hours unless you act now.
To keep it open, click the link below and type your username, your password and your parent's card number.
Link: roboparts-account-check.example.com
Use a computer, not a phone, so the page works correctly.
As a thank-you, the first 50 customers who reply will win a free rover kit worth $200.
Do not tell anyone about this email, because the prize is only for you.
If you do not click today, all of your saved orders and reward points will be deleted.
Thank you, The RoboParts Team
Sent from: rp-prizes-99@example.com
P.S. Reply with your home address so we can mail your prize.

passages.title: System Update
sentences: Sam is drawing a train map on his tablet after dinner.
This box pops up over his drawing.

visual.title: System Update 8.2 Is Ready
rows: This update fixes problems and makes your tablet safer to use.
Download size: 1.2 GB. Installing takes about 25 minutes.
Your tablet will restart two times during the update. Each time, the screen may stay black for up to 2 minutes. This is normal.
Do not turn off your tablet while the update is installing.
Your battery must be at 50% or more, or the tablet must be plugged in.
All open apps will close when the update starts. Save your work first, or you may lose your changes.
You cannot use your tablet until the update is finished.
Your drawings, photos and games will still be there after the update.
After the update, type your passcode once to unlock the tablet.
Choose Install Tonight to update at 2:00 AM while you sleep. Leave the tablet plugged in overnight.
If the update stops before it finishes, keep the tablet plugged in. It will try again by itself.

passages.title: The Dinosaur App
sentences: Ben gets a new dinosaur app called DinoWalk.
A box pops up when he opens it.

visual.title: Allow DinoWalk to use your camera?
rows: DinoWalk uses your camera to show a dinosaur in your room.
Meet a Velociraptor! It was about as big as a turkey.
DinoWalk can also take photos of you with the dinosaur.

passages.title: Platform Safety
sentences: Sam and Grandma Rose wait for the train at Harbor Town Station.
Sam reads the sign on the platform.

visual.title: Platform Safety
rows: Stand behind the yellow line until the train stops.
Some trains pass this platform without stopping. They go fast and make a strong wind.
Let people get off the train before you get on.
Watch the gap between the train and the platform when you step on.
If you drop something on the tracks, do not climb down. Tell a station worker in an orange vest.
Dogs must be on a short leash or in a carrier.

passages.title: Touch Tank Rules
sentences: Maya and Priya visit the Harbor Town Aquarium.
They stop at the touch tank.

visual.title: Touch Tank Rules
rows: Rinse your hands with plain water before you touch. Lotion and sunscreen can harm the animals.
Touch gently with two fingers.
Keep the animals in the water. Do not lift them out.
You may touch the sea stars and the hermit crabs' shells.
Do not touch the sea urchins. Their spines are sharp.
Wash your hands with soap after you touch.
Questions? Ask a staff member in a blue shirt.

passages.title: The Star Show
sentences: Sam's class visits the planetarium at Lantern Peaks Observatory.
A notice hangs on the door of the dome.

visual.title: Star Show: Please Read
rows: The star show lasts 40 minutes. The dome gets very dark.
Near the end of the show, there are bright flashing lights for about 5 minutes.
If flashing lights bother you, ask for a seat by the exit door. You may step out and come back in.
If you need to leave, follow the small blue lights on the floor. Walk slowly.
No phones or flashlights during the show. Their light makes it hard for others to see the stars.
Food and drinks stay in the lobby.

passages.title: Thunderstorm Warning
sentences: Ana and Ben have soccer practice at Pier Field at 4:30 PM.
At 3:05 PM, this alert pops up on their mom's phone.

visual.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning
rows: Harbor Town Weather Service: Severe Thunderstorm Warning until 6:00 PM today.
Storms will reach Harbor Town at about 4:00 PM, with lightning, heavy rain and strong wind.
When you hear thunder, go inside a building or a car with a hard metal roof right away.
Do not wait under a tree, a picnic shelter or a dugout. They do not keep you safe from lightning.
Stay inside until 30 minutes after the last thunder you hear.
All outdoor games and practices in Harbor Town are canceled from 3:30 PM to 6:00 PM.
Tap Details to see the storm map. Tap Dismiss to close this alert.

passages.title: The Free Trial
sentences: Leo wants to listen to music while he skates.
He opens a music app called TuneTide, and this box appears.

visual.title: Try TuneTide Plus FREE!
rows: Play any song with no ads, even with no internet.
Your first 7 days are free.
After 7 days, you pay $9 every month until you cancel.
To start, add a card number. Nothing is charged today.
To stop paying, cancel in Settings before day 7 ends.
Or keep TuneTide Free: play songs with short ads between them, for $0.
Hurry! This offer ends in 2 hours!

passages.title: Tunnel Tour Safety
sentences: Maya visits the Ridgeway Mine Museum with her dad.
Before the tunnel tour, they read this sign at the gate.

visual.title: Ridgeway Mine: Tunnel Tour Safety
rows: Everyone must wear a hard hat in the tunnel. Pick one up at the gate.
Wear closed shoes. The tunnel floor is wet and uneven.
No closed shoes? Borrow a pair of rubber boots at the gate.
The tunnel stays at about 50°F all year. Bring a jacket, even in summer.
Stay on the path between the yellow ropes. The old side tunnels are closed.
Do not pick up rocks in the tunnel. You may take one rock from the Free Rock Bin at the gift shop.
Visitors under 12 must stay next to their adult for the whole tour.
If the tunnel lights go out, stand still. Your guide will turn on the backup lights.

passages.title: The Tide Board at Gull Point
sentences: Sam, Pixel and Grandma Rose reach Gull Point at 11:40 AM.
They read the board by the beach stairs.

visual.title: Gull Point Beach: Today's Tides and Warnings
rows: Low tide: 12:30 PM. High tide: 6:45 PM.
Tide pools are open from 2 hours before low tide until 1 hour after low tide.
After that, the rising water covers the path back to the stairs.
Rip current warning: no swimming at the north end, by the red flags.
A rip current is a strong, narrow stream of water that flows away from the shore.
If a current pulls you, swim sideways, along the beach, not against it. Then wave to a lifeguard.
Swim only between the green flags. Lifeguards are there from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
Dogs must be on a leash. Dogs are not allowed in the tide pools.
Look at sea stars and crabs, then leave them where you found them.

credit.title: The Tide Board at Gull Point
credit.author: Learning to Fly (AI-drafted)

passages.title: Story Woods Trail Notice
sentences: From April 1 to June 15, the Creek Trail in Story Woods is closed between the old mill and the campsite.
A pair of great blue herons has built a large nest of sticks high in a pine tree beside the trail.
Herons are easily disturbed while they are nesting, and if people walk too close, the parents may leave and the eggs can get cold.
Park rangers have put up a rope fence and orange signs at both ends of the closed section.
Hikers can still reach the campsite by using the Ridge Trail, which is the only other route.
The Ridge Trail is 1.5 miles longer than the Creek Trail, and it climbs a steep, rocky hill.
Allow about 45 extra minutes of walking, and carry additional water on warm afternoons.
Cyclists may use the Ridge Trail, but they must walk their bikes up the steepest section.
During the nesting season, dogs must remain on a leash on every trail in Story Woods.
Visitors who would like to observe the herons can use the viewing deck behind the old mill.
The deck is about 300 feet from the nest, a distance that keeps the birds calm.
Free binoculars hang on hooks at the deck, and a ranger answers questions there on Saturday mornings.
Please speak quietly on the deck, and never use a camera flash, because a sudden light can startle the birds.
The trail may reopen early if the young herons leave the nest before June 15.
Rangers will post any change on the information board in the Story Woods parking lot.
Thank you for helping the herons raise their chicks in peace.

items.prompt: Maya wants to keep her comic. Which button should she tap?
options: Delete
Cancel
items.hint: Read the line that tells what happens after Delete.
items.explain: Maya should tap Cancel. The box says you cannot get the file back after Delete, and Cancel stops it.

items.prompt: This box pops up on Sam's tablet. What should Sam do?
options: Plug in his tablet
Turn up the sound
Start a new game
items.hint: Find the line in the box that tells you what to do.
items.explain: Sam should plug in his tablet. The box says to plug in your tablet soon.

items.prompt: Tap the thing Sam needs for his tablet.
items.hint: Read what the box says to do. Which thing helps you do that?
items.explain: Sam needs the charger. The box says to plug in the tablet, and the charger plugs it in.

items.prompt: Maya is not sure she wants to delete her comic. Tap the button that keeps it safe.
items.hint: Read both buttons. Which one stops the delete?
items.explain: Tap Cancel. Cancel stops the delete, so the comic stays. When you are not sure, keep the file.

items.prompt: Tap the bowl Ben should use for his soup.
items.hint: Read the label again. Which kind of bowl does it say to use?
items.explain: Ben should use the microwave-safe bowl. The label says to use a bowl that says microwave safe, and no metal.

items.prompt: Ben is not sure if his bowl is safe. What should he do?
options: Ask an adult
Use it anyway
items.hint: Find the line that tells you what to do when you are not sure.
items.explain: Ben should ask an adult. The last line says to ask an adult if you are not sure.

items.prompt: This box asks to know where Sam is. What should Sam do?
options: Tap Allow right away
Tap the map behind the box
Ask an adult first
items.hint: Read what the app wants. Is it asking for private information about you?
items.explain: Sam should ask an adult first. The box asks to know where he is, and you ask an adult before you allow that.

items.prompt: Sam shows the box to his mom. Tap the line that tells her what the app wants.
items.hint: Read the lines above the buttons. Find the one that says what the app is asking for.
items.explain: Tap the first line. It says Trail Tracker wants to know where Sam is.

items.prompt: Priya wants to keep her new changes. Which button should she tap?
options: Don't Save
Cancel
Save
items.hint: Read the question in the box. Which button answers yes to it?
items.explain: Priya should tap Save. The box asks to save your changes before closing, and Save keeps them.

items.prompt: Priya wants to stay in the file and keep working. Tap the button that takes her back.
items.hint: One button stops the closing. Read all three buttons.
items.explain: Tap Cancel. Cancel stops the file from closing, so Priya can keep working.

items.prompt: Ben wants to update now. What must he do first?
options: Plug in his tablet
Turn off the sound
Tap Later
items.hint: Find the line with the word before.
items.explain: Ben must plug in his tablet first. The last line says to plug in your tablet before you update.

items.prompt: Put Ben's steps in order.
items.hint: Find the word before in the box. Then think about what comes after the update.
items.explain: First Ben plugs in the tablet. Then he taps Update Now and waits about 10 minutes. Last, he plays. The box says to plug in before you update.

items.prompt: What should Leo do about this box?
options: Tap Claim Prize fast
Close the box and tell an adult
Type his home address
items.hint: Look for clues. Does the box rush you? Does it ask for private things?
items.explain: Leo should close the box and tell an adult. The box rushes him and asks for his home address. A pop-up that promises a prize is a trick.

items.prompt: Leo keeps his home address private. Tap the line in the box that asks for it.
items.hint: Read each line. Look for words about where you live.
items.explain: Tap the last line. It asks Leo to type his name and home address. That is private, so he closes the box.

items.prompt: What should Ben do about this chat?
options: Send his password to get the gems
Send only half of his password
Keep his password secret and tell an adult
items.hint: Find what the player asks Ben to send. Is that something you share?
items.explain: Ben should keep his password secret and tell an adult. The third message asks for his password. Never share a password, even for free gems.

items.prompt: Ben shows the chat to his mom. Tap the message that asks for something private.
items.hint: Read each message. Find the one that asks Ben to send something.
items.explain: Tap the third message. It asks for Ben's password, and a password is private.

items.prompt: Sam wants to tap each of these on his tablet. Sort them using the rules.

cards.text: Tap OK on a low battery box
Tap Allow so an app can use the camera
Tap Save on your comic
Tap Buy for 100 gems ($5)
Tap Allow so an app can see your location

items.hint: Match each card to a rule. Does the rule start with You can, or with Ask an adult?
items.explain: Tapping OK on low battery and tapping Save are OK by the first two rules. Tapping Allow and buying gems need an adult first, by the rules about Allow and buying.

items.prompt: A prize box covers Sam's game. Mom is at work. Tap the two things Sam should do, in order.
items.hint: Find the rule about prizes. It has two steps. Look for the word Then.
items.explain: First Sam closes the box. Then he texts Mom to tell an adult. The last rule says to close a prize box and then tell an adult.

items.prompt: Sam wants to keep his ears safe. Tap the button he should press.
items.hint: Read the line about your hearing. Then read both buttons.
items.explain: Tap Lower Volume Now. The box says loud sound for a long time can hurt your hearing, so a lower volume keeps Sam's ears safe.

items.prompt: Sam does not tap either button. What will happen in 30 seconds?
options: The volume will go down by itself.
The podcast will stop.
The tablet will turn off.
The volume will get louder.
items.hint: Find the line with the number 30. Read what it says will happen.
items.explain: The volume will go down by itself. The third line says this happens in 30 seconds if you do nothing.

items.prompt: Maya's mom says, "People you have never met should not be able to message you or find out where you live." Which two settings should Maya change?
options: Who can send me messages, and Add my town to each drawing I post
Let the app use my camera, and Find friends from my contacts list
Show ads based on what I draw, and Who can see my drawings
Find friends from my contacts list, and Add my town to each drawing I post
items.hint: Mom names two worries: messages from people you have never met, and where you live. Find the setting for each worry. Read the note to see what Everyone means.
items.explain: Maya should change Who can send me messages and Add my town to each drawing I post. Messages are set to Everyone, which the note says includes people she has never met, and adding her town tells people where she lives.

items.prompt: Maya and her mom pick a choice for each setting. Sort the choices.

cards.text: Who can send me messages: Friends
Who can send me messages: Everyone
Add my town: Off
Add my town: On
Let the app use my camera: Ask every time
Let the app use my camera: Always

items.hint: For each card, ask two questions. Can people I have never met reach me or find me? Can the app do something without asking me first?
items.explain: Friends for messages, town Off and camera Ask every time are the safer choices. Everyone, town On and camera Always let more people reach or find Maya, or let the app use the camera without asking. Each choice is in the rows for messages, town and camera.

items.prompt: Ben is 12 years old. He wants the Big pack. What is the safe thing to do?
options: Tap Buy Now, because the Big pack is the best value
Tap Ask a Parent, so a parent can say yes or no first
Buy the Small pack instead, because it costs only $1
Tap Buy Now and tell a parent about it tomorrow
items.hint: Find the line about players under 13. Then find the button that does what that line needs.
items.explain: Ben should tap Ask a Parent. He is under 13, so a parent must approve each purchase, and Ask a Parent sends a request with no charge until a parent says yes.

items.prompt: Ben wants the Rocket Drill. His mom says no to buying gems this week. What can he do instead?
options: Tap Buy Now on the Small pack
Finish the Daily Build on 3 days
Finish the Daily Build on 5 days
Tap Ask a Parent again for the Big pack
items.hint: First work out how many more gems Ben needs. Then find the line about free gems and count the days.
items.explain: Ben can finish the Daily Build on 3 days. The last line says he has 40 gems and the Rocket Drill costs 100, so he needs 60 more. The free gems line says he earns 20 each day, and 20 + 20 + 20 = 60.

items.prompt: Ben is signing in on his new laptop, so he types the code. Then a player sends him a chat: "I work for Block Builder. Tell me your code so I can check your account." What should Ben do?
options: Tell the player the code, because he works for Block Builder
Keep the code secret and show the chat to his mom
Tell the player only half of the code
Wait 10 minutes, then tell the player the old code
items.hint: Find the line that says who may ask for the code. Compare it with what the player says.
items.explain: Ben should keep the code secret and show the chat to his mom. The fourth line says never to tell the code to anyone, and Block Builder staff will never ask for it in a chat.

items.prompt: Ben is at soccer practice when this text comes. Nobody at home is using his laptop. What should Ben and his mom do?
options: Type the code on the sign-in screen
Not type the code, then tap Secure My Account and change the password together
Send the code back to Block Builder in a text
Do nothing, because the code stops working in 10 minutes
items.hint: First decide: is Ben the one signing in? Then find the line for that case.
items.explain: They should not type the code, and they should tap Secure My Account and change the password together. Ben is not the one signing in, and the fifth line tells what to do when it is not you.

items.prompt: Priya checks the email for clues. Sort each part.
bins: Clue that it is a trick
Could be in a real email too

cards.text: Says the account will close in 24 hours unless she acts now
Asks for her password and a card number
Tells her to keep the email a secret
Promises a free $200 rover kit
Uses the shop's name, RoboParts
Says it is sorry for the trouble
Is signed The RoboParts Team

items.hint: For each card, ask: does it rush me, ask for a password or money, promise a big prize, or ask me to keep a secret? If not, any email could say it.
items.explain: Rushing her, asking for her password and a card number, promising a big prize and asking for a secret are clues that it is a trick. Using the shop's name, saying sorry and signing as the team could be in any email, so they do not prove it is real.

items.prompt: What should Priya do with this email?
options: Click the link quickly, before the 24 hours are up
Reply with only her username, not her password
Show it to a parent and not click the link
Send it to her friends so they can win a rover kit too
items.hint: Look at what the email asks her to type and what it asks her to keep secret. Then think about the rule for passwords.
items.explain: Priya should show it to a parent and not click the link. The email asks for her password and a card number and tells her to keep it a secret. A real shop never asks for a password in an email.

items.prompt: Sam's battery is at 35%, and his map is not saved. He needs the tablet for homework in 20 minutes. What is the best plan?
options: Tap Install Now, because 35% battery is enough
Save the map, tap Install Tonight, and plug the tablet in before bed
Tap Install Now, and save the map while the update runs
Tap Install Now, and turn the tablet off if the screen goes black
items.hint: Check four things: how long the update takes, how much battery it needs, what happens to open apps, and when he needs the tablet. Then find the plan that fits all four.
items.explain: Sam should save his map, tap Install Tonight and plug the tablet in before bed. The update needs 50% battery or a plug, closes open apps, and takes about 25 minutes, but he needs the tablet in 20 minutes.

items.prompt: Sam chose Install Tonight. He wakes up at 2:10 AM and sees that his tablet screen is black. What should he do?
options: Leave it plugged in and go back to sleep, because a black screen during a restart is normal
Hold the power button to turn the tablet off
Unplug the tablet, because the update must be finished
Tap Remind Me Later to stop the update
items.hint: Find the line about the screen going black. Then find the line about turning the tablet off.
items.explain: Sam should leave it plugged in and go back to sleep. The box says the screen may stay black for up to 2 minutes during each restart, that this is normal, and not to turn the tablet off while it installs.

items.prompt: What does DinoWalk want to use?
options: The camera
The microphone
Your location
items.hint: Read the first line in the box. Find the word that names a part of the tablet.
items.explain: DinoWalk wants to use the camera. The first line says it uses your camera to show a dinosaur in your room.

items.prompt: Ben's mom is busy. Ben wants to see the Velociraptor right now. What should he do?
options: Tap Allow now and tell his mom later
Wait and ask his mom before he taps Allow
Tap the dinosaur to take a photo
items.hint: Read what the box asks for. Is the camera something you allow by yourself?
items.explain: Ben should wait and ask his mom before he taps Allow. The box asks to use his camera, and you ask an adult before you allow an app to use it.

items.prompt: Sam's map falls off the platform onto the tracks. What should he do?
options: Climb down fast and get it before a train comes
Lie down at the edge and reach for it
Tell a station worker in an orange vest
Ask Grandma Rose to climb down for it
items.hint: Find the line that starts with If you drop something. Read both parts of it.
items.explain: Sam should tell a station worker in an orange vest. The fifth line says not to climb down and to tell a station worker.

items.prompt: Put Sam's steps in order to get on the train safely.
steps: Let people get off the train.
Watch the gap and step on.
items.hint: Look for the words until and before in the rules. They tell you what comes first.
items.explain: First Sam stands behind the yellow line until the train stops. Then he lets people get off, and last he watches the gap as he steps on. The order comes from the first, third and fourth rules.

items.prompt: Priya reads the rules. Sort each thing she might do.

cards.text: Touch a sea star with two fingers
Lift a hermit crab out of the water
Touch a sea urchin
Rinse her hands with plain water first
Wash her hands with soap at the end
Put on sunscreen just before she touches

items.hint: Match each card to one rule. Does the rule say to do it, or say not to?
items.explain: Touching a sea star with two fingers, rinsing with water first and washing with soap at the end follow the rules. Lifting a crab out, touching an urchin and putting on sunscreen right before break the rules about keeping animals in the water, sharp spines and lotion or sunscreen.

items.prompt: Maya just put lotion on her hands. She wants to touch a sea star. What should she do?
options: Touch the sea star right away with two fingers
Rinse her hands with plain water, then touch gently with two fingers
Ask a staff member to lift the sea star out for her
Touch it with one finger, so less lotion gets on it
items.hint: Find the rule about lotion. Then find the rule about how to touch.
items.explain: Maya should rinse her hands with plain water, then touch gently with two fingers. The first rule says lotion can harm the animals, and the second says to touch with two fingers.

items.prompt: Bright flashing lights bother Maya. What can she do before the show starts?
options: Bring her flashlight into the dome
Sit in the middle of the dome
Ask for a seat by the exit door
Hold up her phone to block the light
items.hint: Find the line that starts with If flashing lights bother you.
items.explain: Maya can ask for a seat by the exit door. The third line says this, and it says she may step out and come back in.

items.prompt: Sam needs to leave during the show. How should he find the way out?
options: Turn on his phone light
Follow the small blue lights on the floor and walk slowly
Run to the door before the lights flash
Ask a friend to shine a flashlight
items.hint: Find the line about leaving. Then check the line about phones and flashlights.
items.explain: Sam should follow the small blue lights on the floor and walk slowly. The fourth line says this, and the fifth line says no phones or flashlights during the show.

items.prompt: What does this alert mean for Ana and Ben's practice at 4:30 PM?
options: Practice is still on, because the warning ends at 6:00 PM
Practice is canceled, because outdoor practices stop from 3:30 PM to 6:00 PM
Practice moves into the picnic shelter at the field
Practice starts early, at 3:30 PM, before the storm comes
items.hint: Find the line about outdoor games and practices. Check whether 4:30 PM is inside its times.
items.explain: Practice is canceled. The sixth line cancels outdoor practices from 3:30 PM to 6:00 PM, and 4:30 PM is between those times.

items.prompt: The last thunder was at 5:55 PM. At 6:10 PM, the rain has stopped and the warning is over. When is it safe for the twins to kick a ball in the yard?
options: Right away, because the warning ended at 6:00 PM
Right away, because the rain has stopped
At 6:25 PM
At 6:55 PM
items.hint: The rain and the warning are not the rule here. Find the line about the last thunder, then add the minutes it gives.
items.explain: It is safe at 6:25 PM. The fifth line says to stay inside until 30 minutes after the last thunder, and 5:55 PM plus 30 minutes is 6:25 PM.

items.prompt: The storm reaches the skate park. Leo hears thunder. Tap the safest place for him to go.

objects.label: The dugout by the ball field
The library building across the street

items.hint: Read the line about where to go when you hear thunder. Then read the line about places that are not safe.
items.explain: Leo should go to the library building. The alert says to go inside a building, and it says a tree, a picnic shelter and a dugout do not keep you safe from lightning.

items.prompt: Suppose Leo starts the free trial and forgets to cancel. What happens after 7 days?
options: The trial ends, and nothing is charged
The card is charged $9 one time only
He gets 7 more free days
The card is charged $9, and then $9 again every month
items.hint: Find the line that starts with After 7 days. Then find the line that tells how to stop paying.
items.explain: The card is charged $9, and then $9 again every month. The third line says you pay $9 every month until you cancel, and the fifth line says you must cancel before day 7 ends to stop paying.

items.prompt: Leo checks the box before he taps anything. Sort each part.
bins: A reason to slow down and ask an adult

cards.text: It asks for a card number
It says the offer ends in 2 hours
It charges $9 every month after day 7
You must remember to cancel to stop paying
TuneTide Free has short ads between songs
TuneTide Free costs $0

items.hint: For each card, ask: does it rush me, or could it cost real money? If yes, slow down and ask an adult.
items.explain: The card number, the 2-hour rush, the $9 every month and the need to cancel are reasons to slow down and ask an adult, because they rush Leo or cost real money. The lines about TuneTide Free are plain information about the $0 choice.

items.prompt: Leo wants music today. He cannot spend any money, and no adult is home to ask. Which choice is safe?
options: Tap Start Free Trial, then cancel tomorrow
Tap Keep TuneTide Free
Tap Start Free Trial, because nothing is charged today
Tap Start Free Trial and use a card number he finds at home
items.hint: Leo has two conditions: no money, and no adult to ask. Check what each button needs before it works.
items.explain: Leo should tap Keep TuneTide Free. The free trial needs a card number, which means real money and an adult. TuneTide Free plays songs for $0.

items.prompt: Maya is 11, and she is wearing sandals. What must she do to go on the tunnel tour?
options: Wear a hard hat and walk at the front with the guide
Borrow rubber boots, wear a hard hat, and stay next to her dad
Borrow rubber boots and a hard hat, then walk the tour by herself
Skip the tour, because sandals are not allowed in the tunnel
items.hint: Check three rules: the one for everyone, the one about shoes, and the one about age.
items.explain: Maya must borrow rubber boots, wear a hard hat and stay next to her dad. Everyone wears a hard hat, visitors without closed shoes can borrow boots, and visitors under 12 stay next to their adult.

items.prompt: Maya sees a shiny gold-colored rock on the tunnel floor. She wants a rock to take home. What should she do?
options: Pick it up, because it might be real gold
Step past the yellow ropes to look for a bigger one
Ask the guide to pick it up for her
Leave it there, and take one rock from the Free Rock Bin at the gift shop
items.hint: Find the rule about rocks. It has two parts: what not to do, and what you may do instead.
items.explain: Maya should leave it there and take one rock from the Free Rock Bin. The rule says not to pick up rocks in the tunnel, and you may take one rock from the bin at the gift shop.

items.prompt: They reach Gull Point at 11:40 AM. What is the latest time they can stay at the tide pools?
items.hint: Find the time of low tide. Then read the rule about when the tide pools close, and add the time it gives.
items.explain: They can stay until 1:30 PM. Low tide is at 12:30 PM, and the tide pools are open until 1 hour after low tide. After that, the water covers the path back to the stairs.

items.prompt: Grandma Rose wants to swim after lunch. Which plan follows the board?
options: Swim between the green flags at 5:30 PM
Swim between the green flags at 3:00 PM
Swim by the red flags at 3:00 PM
Swim at the north end at 11:00 AM
items.hint: A safe swim needs two things: the right place and the right time. Check each plan for both.
items.explain: She should swim between the green flags at 3:00 PM. The board says to swim only between the green flags, and lifeguards are there from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The red flags at the north end mark the rip current.

items.prompt: Sam, Pixel and Grandma Rose spend the day at Gull Point. Sort what they do.

cards.text: Pixel walks on a leash on the sand
Pixel splashes in a tide pool
Sam looks at a crab, then leaves it in its pool
Sam takes a sea star home in a bucket
They stay on the rocks until 2:00 PM
They walk back up the stairs at 1:15 PM

items.hint: Match each card to a rule about dogs, animals or tide pool times. For the times, work out when the tide pools close.
items.explain: Walking Pixel on a leash, leaving the crab and going back at 1:15 PM follow the board. Pixel in a tide pool, taking a sea star and staying until 2:00 PM break the rules, because dogs stay out of the pools, animals stay where you found them, and the pools close at 1:30 PM.

items.prompt: On May 10, Sam wants to walk with Pixel from the old mill to the campsite. Which plan follows the notice?
options: Take the Creek Trail with Pixel on a leash, because leashed dogs are allowed
Take the Ridge Trail with Pixel on a leash, and allow about 45 extra minutes
Take the Ridge Trail, and let Pixel off the leash on the steepest section
Wait until June 15, because every trail in Story Woods is closed
items.hint: Check the dates of the closing first. Then find the other way to the campsite and the rule for dogs.
items.explain: Sam should take the Ridge Trail with Pixel on a leash and allow about 45 extra minutes. May 10 is inside the closing, the second paragraph names the Ridge Trail as the only other route and gives the extra time, and dogs must remain on a leash on every trail.

items.prompt: Maya wants to draw the herons. Which plan follows the notice?
options: Walk past the rope fence to get a closer view of the nest
Go to the viewing deck, take photos with a flash, and draw from the photos
Wait at the parking lot board until the trail opens
Go to the viewing deck behind the old mill, borrow binoculars, and draw quietly
items.hint: Read the paragraph about seeing the herons. Check each plan against every rule in it.
items.explain: Maya should go to the viewing deck, borrow binoculars and draw quietly. The third paragraph says to visit the deck, that free binoculars hang there, and to speak quietly and never use a camera flash.

items.prompt: Leo asks why people must stay away from the nest. Tap the sentence that gives the reason.
items.hint: Read the first paragraph. Look for a sentence that says what could happen if people walk too close.
items.explain: Tap the sentence that says herons are easily disturbed while nesting, and if people walk too close, the parents may leave and the eggs can get cold. It is in the first paragraph.

steps.say: Maya wants to keep her comic. So I need the button that keeps it.
I read the box. It asks if she wants to delete Comic Page 3.
The next line says you cannot get it back. Delete means it is gone for good.
Cancel means stop. Nothing gets deleted.
So Maya taps Cancel. When I am not sure, I keep the file.
